newsitem.title: GREECE: ATHLETICS-BAGACH SURPRISES EVEN HIMSELF WITH SHOT PUT TITLE.
newsitem.headline: ATHLETICS-BAGACH SURPRISES EVEN HIMSELF WITH SHOT PUT TITLE.

text.p: Veteran Aleksandr Bagach surprised even himself by upsetting the favourites to win the shot put title on the opening evening of the world championships on Saturday.
The 30-year-old Bagach, who fought many battles for the Soviet Union and now represents Ukraine, equalled his personal best by recording 21.47 metres at his third attempt.
Defending champion John Godina, who was given a wild card to compete, was leading with a mark of 21.44 metres when Bagach moved in front.
American Godina had to be content with silver while Oliver-Sven Buder of Germany took the bronze by beating his previous personal best mark with an effort of 21.24 metres at his final attempt.
"I still can't believe what has happened to me," said Bagach, whose career has been marred by an embarrassing doping case. "I'll probably start realising tomorrow."

Bagach struggled to make his way back to the top after being banned for two years for excessive testosterone levels following third place in the 1989 European Cup. As a result, the Soviet team lost their place in the World Cup.

"Those were different times," said Ukraine's team leader Aleksandr Kolenko. "Since, he has totally changed his approach to competition, trying to find a right balance between power and technique. That took time."
His efforts started to bear fruit at the 1993 world championships in Stuttgart where he took bronze, moving up to third place after American Mike Stulce was disqualified for doping.
Godina, who had seen compatriot and main rival Randy Barnes disappear after the morning's qualifying round, said he felt the title should have gone his way.

"I should have won," he said. "It's all my fault but I knew I was strong enough to win. Even before what happened to Randy, I thought I would win gold. The last couple of years have been tough for me and I was really hoping for that title."
Asked what had happened to Olympic champion Barnes, who lost all hope after ending a poor 14th in qualifying, Godina said he did not know.
"I haven't seen him since but anyway, I assume he does not want to talk about it," said Godina. "I was surprised, obviously. Things like that should not happen."
While Godina was still wondering why he had not won, Bagach quietly said he would carry on until the 2000 Olympics in Sydney.
"I'm preparing for that," he said. "I might be a bit old then but today, I feel young."
